job.title: Operations & Membership Officer
job.description:
Operations & Membership Officer

Chirnside Park, VIC

Full time

Interstate and occasional international travel a few times a year



Whether your background is in events, marketing, account management or B2B partnerships, this role is a chance to take your skills into a national peak industry body. You'll coordinate trade shows (with international travel), drive member growth, manage sponsor relationships and deliver marketing campaigns, with a lot of variety from one week to the next. No association experience is needed, just the energy to get stuck in.

The organisation runs industry-leading events, including a flagship triennial trade exhibition, alongside a strong member services and partnerships program. With over 150 Australian-based company members, this is a genuinely varied role working closely with the General Manager, CEO and business partners across the full operations of the association.



What you'll be doing:

  • Delivering clear, timely reporting on acquisition, sponsorship revenue, event performance and marketing engagement.
  • Proactively identifying, targeting and converting new member companies to drive satisfaction, retention and growth.
  • Coordinating the association's presence at domestic and international trade events, from stand design and staffing through to marketing and lead follow-up.
  • Building and nurturing relationships with sponsors and service partners, and pitching new partners that resonate with the membership.
  • Driving member communications across newsletters, LinkedIn, forums and other digital channels, including publications and member content.
  • Managing the association's recurring events calendar, including its flagship exhibition, an annual awards program, and other member gatherings.


What we're looking for:

  • 5+ years' experience in a customer-facing, coordination or business operations role (association, events or B2B environment preferred).
  • Marketing experience (mainly social media and EDM creation).
  • Strong relationship management and communication skills.
  • Ability to work autonomously and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in a professional context.


Great to have (not essential):

  • Background in events coordination or trade exhibition delivery.
  • Exposure to sponsorship or partnership management.
  • Familiarity with the packaging, processing or broader manufacturing sector.


This is a fantastic opportunity for a relationship-driven operator who wants genuine variety, autonomy and the chance to play a key role in the continued success of a peak industry body.



Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience, circa $90,000 to $100,000 plus superannuation, with interstate and occasional international travel a few times a year.

job.title: Senior Insurance and Disputes Specialist | Legal + Insurance
job.description:
Insurance Disputes Specialist | Legal and Insurance Background

About the client

Our client is a Tier 1 global general insurer with a long-standing presence across Australia and New Zealand, writing a broad range of policies through retail and wholesale channels. They are known for technical excellence, strong governance and a genuine commitment to fair customer outcomes. You will join a specialist Complaints and Customer Resolution team that is respected across the business for its expertise.

About the role

You will investigate and resolve complex customer complaints and disputes across retail and wholesale policies in Australia and New Zealand. This is work built for legally minded people: interpreting policy wordings, weighing evidence, drafting reasoned determinations and negotiating outcomes with customers and the external dispute bodies. You will work closely with claims, underwriting and legal, and your findings will directly shape how the business treats its customers. It is a temp contract starting ASAP through to the end of February initially.

Duties

  • Investigate and analyse internal disputes across a range of business lines and prepare clear, well-reasoned responses.
  • Prepare external dispute responses to AFCA in Australia and FSCL in New Zealand, and liaise directly with both bodies.
  • Manage complex property and indemnity disputes, including attending conciliation conferences to negotiate settlements.
  • Draft IDR determinations for referral to the internal Disputes Resolution Committee.
  • Identify themes, root causes and potential compliance breaches, and escalate matters that carry legal or media risk.

Requirements

  • Both legal and insurance experience: a law degree with experience as a practising lawyer in Australia or overseas, plus experience in general insurance, ideally in complaints, IDR/EDR, claims or insurance litigation.
  • Strong legal reasoning, with the ability to interpret policy wordings and apply them to the facts of a matter.
  • Excellent written skills, with experience drafting determinations, legal advice or formal correspondence.
  • Knowledge of AFCA, the General Insurance Code of Practice and ASIC RG 271 is highly regarded. Overseas-qualified lawyers who can get across the Australian framework quickly are encouraged to apply.
  • Candidates with temporary work rights (Working Holiday Visa's) as well as candidates with full work rights are both welcome to apply

How to apply

If you have a legal and insurance background and you are ready to start, apply now and we will be in touch for a confidential chat.

job.title: Customer Success Program Manager (Fortune 500 SaaS)
job.description:
Customer Success Program Manager

$126.6k + Super | 9 month contract | Flexible Hybrid Role | Sydney CBD Based

About the client

Our client is a global Fortune 500 SaaS company whose software platforms is a leader in the Fintech space. With an established presence in Australia, the business works closely with international teams to deliver for its local customers. It values practical problem solving, clear communication and continuous improvement in how work gets done.

About the role

This is a 9-month contract, hands-on individual contributor role delivering Customer Success programs on the ground in Australia. You will take agreed priorities and turn them into practical plans, coordinate the people involved and keep work moving through to completion. Reporting into a UK-based team while working closely with Australian stakeholders, you will be the local driver of delivery. It suits someone who enjoys organising work, solving problems and improving how a business operates.

Duties

  • Plan and deliver local Customer Success projects and program activities from start to finish.
  • Build clear project plans with tasks, owners, deadlines and key milestones.
  • Work with Australian and UK teams to agree priorities and follow up on actions.
  • Track progress, identify delays or risks early and help resolve issues before they escalate.
  • Prepare updates and business reports, and use feedback and data to recommend practical improvements.

Requirements

  • Around 3 to 5 years of experience in project management, program delivery or business operations.
  • Industry experience within large SaaS or Fintech is highly desirable
  • A proven track record of taking projects from planning through to completion.
  • Strong organisation skills and the ability to manage several priorities at once.
  • Confidence working across different teams and adapting when requirements are unclear or priorities change.
  • Working ability with spreadsheets and presentations for reporting and updates.
  • Basic familiarity with AI tools and a willingness to learn how to use approved tools responsibly.
  • Flexibility to attend agreed meetings across Australian and UK time zones.
  • Experience in Customer Success, customer operations or a software or technology business is advantageous, but not essential.

How to apply

If this sounds like the next step for you, we would love to hear from you, hit APPLY NOW for immediate consideration.

job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
Finance Manager
Permanent full-time role
$120k+super
Broadmeadows, Melbourne

  • Lead the full finance function, including AP, AR, payroll and managing the accounts team
  • Own budgeting, company and project cashflow forecasting, and profit and tax planning
  • Clear scope to improve financial systems, reporting dashboards and job management tools

About the Client

Our client is a growing, project-based business in the Industrial sector with a strong focus on commercial performance and compliance. They manage an active pipeline of projects and rely on accurate job costing, cashflow management and reporting to support their growth. The business values proactive, commercially minded people who take ownership and bring ideas for improvement.

About the Role

As Finance Manager, you will lead the end-to-end finance function, from day-to-day accounts through to month-end, reporting and strategic analysis. You will manage the accounts team and own budgeting, forecasting and cashflow at both company and project level. This is a hands-on leadership role where your insights will directly inform decisions on profitability, growth and risk.

Duties

  • Lead the finance function, including accounts payable, accounts receivable and payroll, and manage the accounts team.
  • Deliver the month-end close, accurate financial reporting and performance insights to support decision-making.
  • Manage budgeting, forecasting, project pipeline forecasting and company and project cashflow.
  • Oversee WIP reporting and project financial performance, including revenue recognition and cost control.
  • Ensure compliance with financial and statutory obligations, including payroll, superannuation, payroll tax and WorkCover.

Requirements

  • Proven experience in a Finance Manager or similar role, including managing accounts payable and receivable.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to build credibility with stakeholders at all levels
  • CA, CPA, or equivalent qualification is highly regarded
  • Experience in project-based, construction, engineering, infrastructure, or contracting environments is highly desirable
  • Strong knowledge of accounting principles, financial reporting and compliance requirements.
  • Advanced financial modelling, forecasting and analytical skills.
  • Demonstrated leadership and team management experience.
  • Experience with financial systems, job management software and dashboards.
  • Experience implementing financial systems or process improvements is highly regarded.

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
About the client

Our client is a large Commonwealth government agency delivering essential services to millions of Australians. Its ICT environment supports some of the most significant service delivery systems in the country, and its technology programs have a direct impact on how people access support. The agency works to an established project management framework and places a strong emphasis on governance, quality and stakeholder partnership.

About the role

As Project Manager, you will plan and lead the delivery of complex ICT projects, some with organisation-wide impact, working under the broad direction of senior staff. You will own projects end to end, from design and planning through to implementation and evaluation, while managing budgets, risks and stakeholder expectations. Alongside delivery, you will lead and develop staff and provide expert advice to stakeholders and the agency’s executive. This is a 12 month contract starting in January 2027, with extension options of up to 24 months.

Duties

  • Plan, manage and deliver complex ICT projects in line with the agency’s project management framework, ensuring milestones are met on time and within budget.
  • Develop and maintain Project Management Plans, schedules, status reports and exception reports, and prepare business cases and executive briefs.
  • Manage project budgets, monitor expenditure and oversee related procurement and contract management.
  • Identify, assess, escalate and treat project risks and issues, and track the realisation of project benefits.
  • Build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders at all levels, and lead, coach and manage the performance of project staff.

Requirements

  • Demonstrated experience delivering complex ICT projects, ideally within government or a large enterprise environment.
  • Proven experience managing a project budget, including monitoring expenditure and reporting against it.
  • Strong written communication skills, with a track record of producing Project Management Plans, status reports and schedules.
  • Experience engaging and managing internal and external stakeholders, from frontline staff through to executive level.
  • Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to balance competing priorities and meet tight deadlines.
  • A current Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance or higher is essential and must be held at the time of application.
  • You must be based in Canberra, as regular onsite attendance is required.

How to apply

If this sounds like the right next contract for you, we would love to hear from you, so please apply now.

job.title: Staff Incident Response Commander
job.description:
• 12-month Sydney contract with a global software company
  • Hands-on forensics across Kubernetes, AWS and GCP
  • Senior IC role shaping process, tooling and mentoring


About the client

Our client is a global software and digital media company whose products are used by individuals and enterprises around the world. It's cyber defence centre protects the company’s products, platforms and customers, working closely with engineering, product and partner teams. The incident response team handles serious, high-visibility security events across modern cloud and application environments. It is a team that values sound judgement, composure and genuine technical depth.

About the role

This is one of the most senior incident command roles in the team, and it stays hands-on. You will lead the most complex security incidents from first alert to closure while doing the forensic investigation yourself, across web applications, APIs, containers and multi-cloud infrastructure. You will bring order to incidents that span many internal teams and external partners, and move comfortably between deep technical analysis and clear briefings for senior leadership. Beyond live incidents, you will help shape how the team responds through better process, tooling, exercises and mentoring.

Duties

  • Command complex security incidents across the full response lifecycle, coordinating internal teams, external partners and their security operations centres.
  • Personally investigate web application, API, cloud and container compromises, including credential and data-exposure scenarios.
  • Collect, preserve and analyse forensic evidence across hosts, networks, cloud platforms and large log sources, keeping defensible records throughout.
  • Brief senior leadership clearly under pressure, and assign and drive remediation across multiple teams and organisations.
  • Build tooling for evidence collection at scale, and lead retrospectives, tabletop exercises, training and mentoring for responders and commanders.


Requirements

  • Extensive front-line incident response and digital forensics experience across many major incidents, with proven command of the full incident lifecycle.
  • Hands-on investigation of web application and API compromises, such as broken access control, authentication and authorisation bypass, IDOR, API abuse and CMS exploitation.
  • Cloud-native and container forensics, including Kubernetes and ephemeral infrastructure, with strong AWS and GCP experience across logging, identity and authorisation models.
  • Deep host and network forensics, including Linux internals and Windows and macOS artefacts.
  • EDR at scale (for example CrowdStrike Falcon), complex SIEM analytics, and log and data analysis across large platforms and data warehouses.
  • Scripting in Bash and at least one interpreted language, such as Python.
  • Working knowledge of ISO 27001, SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR and PCI.
  • Willingness to join an on-call rotation and respond to critical events.
  • Highly regarded: Azure, malware triage and reverse engineering, GCFA, GCIH, GNFA or cloud security certifications, and a government or law-enforcement investigation background.


How to apply

If this sounds like the kind of work you do best, we would love to hear from you, apply now.

job.title: IT Applications Administrator
job.description:
About the client

Our client is a major national cultural institution in Canberra, bringing together a world-class museum and an extensive archive. Its work helps Australians understand an important part of the nation’s story and its lasting impact on Australian society. The IT team delivers modern, secure, resilient and user-centred technology services that support daily operations, public-facing digital services and an ongoing program of enterprise transformation.

About the role

As IT Applications Administrator, you will be the technical custodian for the business applications at the heart of the institution’s collection, including its Collection Management System and Digital Asset Management System. Working under broad direction, you will keep these platforms secure, available and well supported, while driving continual improvement across integrations, databases and cloud services. You will work closely with business stakeholders, vendors and technical specialists, so your work directly shapes how the collection is managed and shared. This is a 12-month contract with potential to extend.

Duties

  • Administer, support and continuously improve a portfolio of business applications, including the Collection Management System, Digital Asset Management System and SaaS platforms.
  • Act as technical custodian for designated applications, covering vendor engagement, configuration, release management, lifecycle planning, monitoring and maintenance.
  • Manage integrations and data flows between business applications, databases, cloud services and enterprise platforms.
  • Coordinate application, database and supporting infrastructure upgrades in line with the Information Security Manual (ISM), the Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) and vendor best practice.
  • Document applications and support procedures, and develop and maintain ITSM processes covering standard changes, incident management and problem management.

Requirements

  • Proven experience administering enterprise business applications, including configuration, upgrades, troubleshooting, user support, vendor management and integration with corporate systems.
  • Experience supporting application integrations using APIs, middleware, ETL processes and scripting such as PowerShell, with database platforms including Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle or PostgreSQL.
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365, including Entra ID, Azure SQL Managed Instance, Azure Storage, Azure Monitor and Azure Key Vault.
  • Experience supporting business-critical production applications in Australian Government or another highly regulated environment, including incident, problem, change and release management, disaster recovery and business continuity.
  • Highly developed written and verbal communication skills, including preparing and maintaining complex technical and non-technical documentation.
  • Experience with museum, cultural institution or archival systems, such as Piction, MuseumPlus or equivalent CMS and DAMS platforms, is highly regarded.
  • Negative Vetting 1 security clearance (Australian citizenship required).

How to apply

If this sounds like the right next step for you, we would love to hear from you, so please apply now.
